report.title: 2025 Water Quality Consumer Confidence Report (Published June 2026)

sources_described: Three sources used interchangeably or blended, averaging 15 million gallons per day: the City's system of 20 active deep groundwater wells (500–900 ft aquifers; most of the water), SFPUC Hetch Hetchy System water (snowmelt from the Northern Sierra Nevada; typically serves the area north of Highway 101; fluoridated, blended with unfluoridated well water in 95054), and Valley Water treated surface water from the Rinconada Water Treatment Plant (Calero Reservoir and Sacramento–San Joaquin Delta imports; primarily the south-west portion of the City).

violations: Tier 3 Notice from SFPUC (PDF page 5): because of equipment failure, the San Francisco Regional Water System operated by the SFPUC did not monitor recycled filter backwash water turbidity at its Sunol Valley Water Treatment Plant from June 23 to July 2, 2025; corrected July 3, 2025; no emergency or impact to SFPUC's water quality.

Lead: 'No Santa Clara water sources have exceeded the ACTION LEVEL for lead' (p.5); 2022 residential tap sampling 0 exceedances. In the 2018 school lead testing (33 schools, 172 samples) one sample exceeded the AL: John Sutter Elementary 26 ppb; repeat sampling after plumbing repairs was non-detect (table note 6).
Report states all water meets applicable federal and state drinking-water standards; no MCL violations disclosed.
extraction_notes: All table rows are on PDF page 4 of the 6-page report (the same table is also published as a separate 1-page accessible PDF, saved alongside and used to cross-check). Source-water table columns: 'Analysis for CSC WELL WATER', 'Analysis for VALLEY WATER', 'Analysis for SFPUC' (source_group values copied in the printed capitalisation), each with Range and Average; the SFPUC header adds '[highest running average]'. Distribution-system tables (coliform, E. coli, TTHM, HAA5, chlorine residual, lead/copper, lithium) have no source column -> source_group null; their second standards column is headed 'State MCL' (holds PHG/MRDLG-like values 0.3, 0.2, 4), stored in phg_printed where it is a goal and nulled for coliform (5.0%). Cells printed 'NA' produced no entry (listed in the notes of the sibling entries). Where the average is printed 'ND' but the range shows a detection ('ND - x'), the entry is detected=true with value=range_high and average=null; ranges 'ND - x' use range_low 0. Values printed with '<' (e.g. '< 3 - 11', '<5', '< 20') are below reporting limits: a '<x' range low is stored as x with a note; a row printed entirely '<x' is treated as not detected. Units copied as printed in upper case (PPM, PPB, UNITS). Foaming agents (MBAS) printed in PPB with values 0.022/0.014 against MCL 500 (probably ppm values; copied as printed). Lithium table range 'ND - 10' conflicts with the p.5 narrative that no lithium was detected. Lead/copper residential taps sampled in 2022 (sample_year 2022); school lead testing 2018; all other rows default to sample_year 2025 although the report notes some data may be more than one year old. PFAS entries (page 5) come from the UCMR5 narrative statement, not table rows, and are flagged in notes. Only constituents detected in at least one source appear in the report's table.
